Team — I reviewed Sara's ask and prepared a short set of redline suggestions to the DPA focused on three items: 1) explicit no-training clause, 2) output ownership and derivative carveouts, and 3) subprocessor notification cadence.

Suggested language summary (see attached no-training-clause-template.txt and the redline doc):
- No-Training (proposed): "Redwood shall not use Customer Data, prompts, or model responses for model training, development, or improvement of any machine learning models without Customer's prior written consent. This obligation extends to all subprocessors."
- Output Ownership: "Customer retains exclusive ownership of outputs and any downstream derivatives generated from Customer Data; Redwood grants Customer an irrevocable, perpetual license to any tooling or artifacts generated specifically for Customer escrow."
- Subprocessor Notification: 30-day notice for new subprocessors with classification of processing scope and residency; emergency exceptions to be logged and audited.

I recommend we mark the DPA with these redlines and offer a technical attachment (the ops evidence pack David produced) as operational proof to Legal.

I'll also call out where our standard export-control language can be tightened for onshore-only processing.
